sections.title: Habit and flowering
sections.text: Night-blooming jessamine is an evergreen shrub that can reach about 4 m, native from Mexico to Venezuela and widely cultivated or naturalised in the tropics. Its greenish-white tubular flowers release a strong fragrance at night and are followed by small pale berries.

sections.title: Toxicity and plate
sections.text: All parts are toxic, especially the berries, to people and domestic animals; do not ingest them. The common name “night jasmine” does not mean it is a true jasmine. The plate matches the glossy leaves, tubular flowers and white berries, though the flowers shown in daylight chiefly open at night.
